why.title: Why I built this
why.bookAlt: Your Money or Your Life by Vicki Robin
why.quote: You are trading your life energy for money.
why.paragraph1: After reading <book>Your Money or Your Life</book>, something clicked for me. For most of us earning a wage, money isn't just money, it's our life energy. Every dollar we spend represents hours of our time, our effort, our life traded away.
why.paragraph2: So I built this app. It helps you see your spending in a different way: not just in currency, but in hours of your life. Because sometimes <cost>"$20"</cost> doesn't feel like much, but <time>"2 hours of my life"</time> does. The goal is simple, to help you become more aware of where your money (or really, time) is going, so you can take back control of it.
why.paragraph3: Everything stays on your device, no logins or cloud syncs. Your data is yours. You can also export the data as a simple JSON file if needed. The free version gives you everything you need to get started. Pro unlocks some extra features like unlimited accounts/categories/hourly rates, etc.
why.paragraph4: Hopefully you'll always have control of your money and your life.

closing.title: See what your money really costs.
closing.body: Free, and no account needed. Add your hourly value in a minute and every number gains a second meaning.

websiteAnalytics.title: Website Usage Analytics
paragraphs: On money2time.com, we use PostHog and Google Analytics to measure pseudonymous page views and a limited set of interactions, such as app download clicks, tutorial selection, and contact-form outcomes. These services may use browser storage or cookies and process technical information including approximate region, device and browser type, and referring site. Google Analytics user and event data is retained for up to 14 months.

On the Web Dashboard (app.money2time.com), the same services measure which dashboard pages you open, when a browser is linked or unlinked, whether transfers from your phone and changes you make succeed, and when a Pro feature is offered. Once your phone has sent its data, these events are linked to that phone's random app identifier, so your dashboard and app usage count as one pseudonymous user until you unlink the browser. The dashboard keeps this separate from the rest of money2time.com, so your visits to other pages are not linked to it. Dashboard events never include your financial data, and dashboard visits are never recorded as session replays.
PostHog may also record a small sample of website visits as session replays with every form field masked, and receives a report when a page error occurs.

We do not send contact-form contents, tutorial search text, financial data, account identifiers, full URL query strings, or data for advertising or personalization. The /download redirect does not add your IP address or user-agent string to its analytics event. Website analytics does not load when your browser's Do Not Track setting is enabled.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Money2Time (the App) is a personal finance app that converts your spending into time equivalents based on your hourly wage. Your privacy is important to us. This policy explains what data the App collects, how it is used, and your rights regarding that data.

sections.title: 1. Data Storage & Local-First Design
paragraphs: All your financial data, including transactions, accounts, categories, recurring rules, and wage settings, is stored locally on your device using an on-device database (SQLite). We do not operate servers that store your personal financial information, and the App never syncs your data or backs it up to a server of ours. If you use the optional Web Dashboard (section 6), your phone sends a copy straight to a browser you linked, end-to-end encrypted; our server passes it along without storing it and cannot read it.
If you uninstall the App, all locally stored data is permanently deleted.

subsections.title: Financial Data (Stored Locally Only)
lists: Transaction amounts, dates, categories, notes, and sentiment tags
Account names, types, and balances
Wage and hourly rate information
Recurring transaction rules
Category names and organization
paragraphs: This data never leaves your device unless you explicitly choose to export it, or to send it to a browser you linked with the Web Dashboard.

subsections.title: Random App Identifier
paragraphs: On first launch, the App generates a random unique identifier beginning with m2t_ that is not linked to your name, email, Apple ID, or any personal identity. The same identifier is shared with PostHog, Google Analytics for Firebase, and RevenueCat for product analytics and subscription management, and with any browser you link with the Web Dashboard, whose usage analytics (PostHog and Google Analytics) use it too.

subsections.title: Usage Analytics
paragraphs: We use PostHog and Google Analytics for Firebase to collect pseudonymous usage data linked to this random app identifier so we can understand how the App is used and improve the experience. Analytics does not include financial amounts, transaction details, account balances, notes, receipts, backups, or personally identifiable information.

PostHog also receives crash and error reports, and records a small sample of app sessions as screen recordings so we can find and fix problems. In those recordings everything that shows your information is masked: text, numbers, input fields, charts and any photo you add. Only the app's own design, such as its icons, illustrations and button labels, stays visible. These recordings never show your financial data.
lists: Screen views and feature usage
App events such as transaction created or settings changed
General preferences such as currency, locale, theme, and display mode
Platform such as iOS or Android

sections.title: 3. In-App Purchases & Subscriptions
paragraphs: The App offers an optional premium subscription (Pro) managed through RevenueCat. Payment is processed by Apple or Google. We never receive or store your payment information, credit card details, or Apple ID/Google Account credentials.
RevenueCat receives your subscription status, product identifier, and expiration date to manage your entitlements. This is linked to the random app identifier, not your personal identity.

sections.title: 4. Notifications
paragraphs: The App may request permission to send notifications. All notifications are scheduled locally on your device. No push notifications are sent from external servers. You can deny notification permission or disable notifications at any time in your device Settings.
lists: Daily check-in reminders
Weekly spending summaries
Recurring transaction alerts

sections.title: 5. Device Permissions
paragraphs: The App requests only notification permission to schedule local reminders and summaries. The App does not access your camera, microphone, photo library, contacts, calendar, messages, location, health data, fitness data, other apps, or browsing history.

sections.title: 6. Data Export, Import & Web Dashboard
paragraphs: You can export all your financial data as a JSON file at any time via the App's Settings. The exported file is shared using your device's native sharing functionality. We do not receive or process your exported data.
You can also import data from a previous Money2Time backup or migrate from the Money Manager app. Importing replaces all existing data on your device.

The Web Dashboard is optional. To use it, you open app.money2time.com on a computer and scan the code it shows with the App. Your phone and that browser then agree on an encryption key that only the two of them hold. While the App's Web Dashboard screen and the browser are both open, the App sends the browser a copy of your data (the same data as an export, with the logos, icons and cover photos you added, but not receipt photos or payment QR codes), encrypted end to end with AES-256-GCM. It travels through a server we run on Cloudflare, which passes the encrypted data along as it arrives and does not store it. We cannot read it.

The browser keeps the last copy it received, still encrypted, in its own storage together with the key, until you unlink it in the browser or in the App. Changes you make in the dashboard travel back to your phone, encrypted the same way, and the App saves them only while its Web Dashboard screen is open and only from a browser you allowed to make changes. Your phone also tells the browser whether you have Money2Time Pro, so it can unlock Pro dashboards, and its random app identifier, for the dashboard's usage analytics. There is no account: we keep no email address, and the server that passes your data along keeps no record of which phones and browsers are linked.

sections.title: 7. Data Deletion
paragraphs: You have full control over your data at all times. Reset All Data permanently deletes all transactions, accounts, categories, recurring rules, and wage settings from your device. Reset Transactions Only clears your transaction history while preserving accounts and categories. Uninstalling the App removes the local database and all stored data entirely. Unlinking a browser from the Web Dashboard deletes the copy it keeps: right away when you unlink in the browser, and the next time it connects when you unlink from the App. Clearing that browser's site data deletes it too.

Resetting data within the App does not delete your subscription status held by Apple/Google or analytics data previously sent to PostHog and Google Analytics for Firebase. To request deletion of analytics data, contact us at the email below.

sections.title: 8. Third-Party Services
paragraphs: The App does not display advertisements or use advertising SDKs.

rows: PostHog and Google Analytics for Firebase
Random app ID, feature usage events, preferences
Web Dashboard connection, only if you use it
Your data, end-to-end encrypted and only in transit; connection details such as IP address, kept briefly in Cloudflare's logs

sections.title: 9. Data Security
paragraphs: Your financial data is stored in an unencrypted local database protected by your device's built-in security. When you use the Web Dashboard, it is encrypted on your phone with AES-256-GCM, using a key your phone and browser agree on with P-256 key exchange, and sent over HTTPS; our server never has the key. The App uses only standard, published encryption algorithms.

sections.title: 10. Children's Privacy
paragraphs: The App is not directed at children under the age of 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If you believe a child has provided data through the App, please contact us and we will take steps to remove such information.

sections.title: 11. Changes to This Policy
paragraphs: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Changes will be reflected on this page with an updated Last updated date. Continued use of the App after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.

dataDeletion.title: Data Deletion Request
dataDeletion.intro: Money2Time is a local-first app: all of your financial data is stored only on your device and is never stored on our servers. This page explains how to request deletion of the data associated with the Money2Time app, including the steps to request deletion and which types of data are deleted or kept, along with any retention periods.

subsections.title: Delete data stored on your device
paragraphs: Almost all of your data, including all of your financial data, is stored only on your device. You can delete it yourself at any time:
lists: Open the Money2Time app and go to Settings.
Tap "Reset All Data" to permanently delete all transactions, accounts, categories, recurring rules, and wage settings.
Alternatively, uninstall the app to remove the local database and all stored data entirely.

subsections.title: Delete the copy in a linked browser
paragraphs: If you use the Web Dashboard, each browser you linked keeps the last copy your phone sent it, encrypted. To delete it:
lists: In the browser, open app.money2time.com and choose "Unlink this browser". The copy and its key are deleted at once.
Or, in the Money2Time app, go to Settings > Web Dashboard and tap "Unlink" next to the browser. It deletes its copy the next time it connects.
Clearing the browser's site data for app.money2time.com also deletes it.

subsections.title: Request deletion of analytics and subscription data
paragraphs: To request deletion of analytics or subscription data associated with your random app identifier, contact us:
lists: Email us at the address below with the subject "Data Deletion Request", or use the contact form on this site.
Use the copy button beside User ID in Settings > Display and include the complete ID so we can locate the data associated with your app.
We will process your request and confirm completion within 30 days.

sections.title: What Data Is Deleted or Kept
paragraphs: The table below summarizes what happens to each type of data when you request deletion, and how long any data is retained.

rows: On-device financial data (transactions, accounts, categories, recurring rules, wage settings)
Removed immediately when you reset data or uninstall the app. Nothing is retained by us.
Web Dashboard copy in a browser you linked
Removed from that browser when you unlink it or clear its site data. Our servers never store it, so nothing is retained by us.
Pseudonymous analytics data (PostHog and Google Analytics for Firebase)
Deleted within 30 days of your request.
Retained by Apple or Google for billing, tax, and legal obligations, and managed through your Apple or Google account.

sections.title: Data We Do Not Store
paragraphs: Money2Time does not require an account and does not store your name, email, Apple ID, Google Account, or payment details on our servers. Because your financial data is never stored on our servers, including when you use the Web Dashboard, we cannot access or delete it for you.
Subscription and payment records held by Apple or Google are outside our control and are managed directly through your Apple or Google account.

costInHours.title: What an hour of work buys, country by country
costInHours.intro: Every price has a second number: the time you worked for it. This page sets each country's own published wage against one product that is the same everywhere, so what an hour buys can be compared without first arguing about what went in the basket.

compare.caption: Published pay and the work behind one Big Mac, in two countries

metrics.payPerHourUsd: Pay per hour in US dollars
metrics.bigMacsPerMonth: Big Macs a month's pay buys

allMarkets.title: Every market, ranked
allMarkets.intro: Every country this site is published in, ordered by how long the pay figure has to work for one Big Mac. The third column is worth reading first: a few of these are medians and most are averages, and averages sit higher because the top pulls them up.
allMarkets.caption: Published wage figures and the work behind one Big Mac, ranked by country

method.title: How the hours are worked out
method.body: Where a statistics office publishes an hourly figure, that figure is used as it stands. Where it publishes a weekly or monthly one, it is divided by a {hours}-hour week. Stats NZ happens to publish both, and the two agree to within fifty cents.

basket.title: Why one burger and not a shopping basket
basket.body: A Big Mac, a litre of octane-95 petrol and a household kilowatt-hour are the same things in every country here, each priced by one publisher on one date. Three caveats sit in the data itself: The Economist prices the euro area as one, so its members share a burger price; in India, where McDonald's sells no beef Big Mac, it prices the chicken Maharaja Mac; and Russia has had none since McDonald's left, which the table shows as a gap rather than filling in.

comparability.title: The wages are not strictly comparable
comparability.body: Nobody publishes a single median wage table covering these countries, so every figure comes from its own national statistics office, or from the OECD where it collects them on one basis. A few are medians and most are averages, and they do not all count the same workers. Read the gaps between countries as indicative rather than exact.

grossPay.title: These are before tax
grossPay.body: Published wages are gross. What actually reaches your account is smaller, which means your own hours are longer than the ones on this page.

loan.deleteBody: This will permanently delete this account and all its transactions. This cannot be undone.
loan.name: Account name
loan.interestModelInfo: Reducing balance: interest is charged every month on what you still owe, so paying extra or early cuts the interest you pay. Most home loans work this way. Flat rate: interest is worked out once on the full amount you borrowed and added up front, so paying early clears the debt sooner but saves no interest. Most car and personal loans work this way.
loan.termInfo: How many monthly instalments the loan runs for, up to {max}. A 5 year loan is 60.
loan.termError: Enter a whole number from 1 to {max}.
loan.rateInfoReducing: The yearly rate your bank charges on what you still owe. Type it and the monthly instalment and total are worked out for you, or type the total instead and the rate is worked out.
loan.rateInfoFlat: The yearly flat rate, charged on the full amount you borrowed for the whole loan period. Type it and the monthly instalment and total are worked out for you, or type the total instead and the rate is worked out.
loan.effectiveRateHint: Effective rate {rate}%. That is what this flat rate costs on a reducing balance.
loan.totalRepayableInfo: Everything you pay back over the whole loan: the amount you borrowed plus all the interest.
loan.instalmentInfo: What you pay every month. It follows the total above; turn the switch on if your bank charges a different amount and we use yours exactly.
loan.instalmentErrorLow: Too small to repay the loan within the loan period.
loan.instalmentErrorHigh: Too large for this loan amount and period.
loan.paidPeriodsInfo: Leave at 0 for a new loan. If you are part way through, enter how many instalments you have paid and the opening balance is worked out for you.
loan.paidPeriodsError: Must be fewer than the loan period.
loan.collectInfo: The account the instalment is taken from each month. Pick one and it is recorded automatically; leave it empty and you record each repayment yourself.
loan.collectExternal: This repayment is set up in Recurring. Edit it there.
loan.countAsExpenseInfo: A repayment always moves money into the loan, so what you owe keeps falling either way. With this on it also counts as spending in your totals, budgets and charts, filed under the category you pick. Turn it off and repayments stay out of your spending. Changing it later only affects repayments recorded from then on.
loan.startDateInfo: When the loan was taken out. The first instalment falls one month later, and its day of month becomes your payment day.
loan.balanceOwedInfo: What you still owe today, without the interest you have not been charged yet. It is normally smaller than the figure on your statement.
loan.includeInTotalsHint: Hidden accounts are excluded from total balance.
loan.archiveHint: Hides it from your accounts list. History and totals are kept, and "Show archived" brings it back.
loan.rateChangeTitle: When does the new rate apply?
loan.rateChangeMessage: The rate is changing from {from}% to {to}%. Apply it from today to keep the interest already charged as it is, or from the start if you are correcting a mistake.
loan.currencyChangeMessage: The balance will be converted from {from} to {to} at the latest rate. Existing entries keep their original currency.

loan.balancePromptMessage: Balance changed by {amount}. Record as income/expense or keep as account difference (excluded from insights totals).
loan.balanceOwedHint: Your statement may show {amount}, which adds the interest still to come.
